blocking.issue: The new Bounds rule credits Control plane and GitOps with proposing the 64 MiB and 30 s fetch limits for Nodes and the CLI, but that document does not do so. It applies them only to Ruralz Control's online Plugin check, and nothing there mentions Node or CLI fetches, referrers or Sigstore bundles. Someone implementing the Node or CLI verifier who follows the link will find no limit for their path, so the ADR and its dependency now disagree about who owns the bound. This is a new regression introduced by the L1-4 fix. The per-referrer limits in the ADR (16, 1 MiB, 10 s) are fine; only the attribution is false.
blocking.evidence: ADR, Decision outcome, Bounds: "Verifiers list only Sigstore bundle referrers and try at most 16 of at most 1 MiB each within 10 s (target), inside the 64 MiB and 30 s fetch limits (target) of [Control plane and GitOps](../architecture/04-control-plane-and-gitops.md#building-and-recording-a-revision), proposed there for Nodes and the CLI." 04-control-plane-and-gitops.md, Building and recording a Revision (line 236), the only statement of these limits: "The online Plugin check dials only allowlisted registries, binds credentials to one host, follows no redirects and stops at 64 MiB or 30 s (target)."
blocking.fix: Make the ADR the source of the extension, not Control plane and GitOps. Replace "inside the 64 MiB and 30 s fetch limits (target) of [Control plane and GitOps](...#building-and-recording-a-revision), proposed there for Nodes and the CLI." with "inside the 64 MiB and 30 s fetch limits (target) that [Control plane and GitOps](...#building-and-recording-a-revision) sets for the online Plugin check, which this ADR extends to Nodes and the CLI." This adds about 7 words, and the body is at about 1,499 of 1,500, so trim the same amount elsewhere. For example, shorten the Figure 1 caption to "*Figure 1: signers and Node verification points.*". Do not trim the L1-1 to L1-4 text or the degraded-metric example.

non_blocking.suggestion: Bounds: "Results are cached by artifact digest and trust policy version". A file-mode trust policy in process configuration has no `version`; only anchor sets do. Key the cache by a content hash of the effective trust policy, including the Sigstore trusted root, so a publisher removal or root refresh invalidates it in both modes.

Trust policies: "which without one fail with RZ-CFG-033 naming the missing input". Limit this to Bundles that reference a Plugin (or to a pushed Revision). Otherwise a Plugin-free Bundle fails `ruralz bundle build` in CI for want of a trust policy it never uses.

Bounds: with a 16-referrer cap, a registry writer can attach 16 junk referrers so the valid signature is never tried. The result fails closed, which is correct, but the verifier could list referrers newest first, or try those whose certificate identity matches the trust policy first, so a leftover junk referrer does not cause a deterministic NACK.

Offline verification: Rekor v2 gives no integrated log timestamp, so in practice the "trusted timestamp" comes from an RFC 3161 timestamp authority. Say so in a few words so the verifier is configured to require signed timestamps rather than observer or log time.

foundation_amendments: Pack 8.14: name the trust policy source for `ruralz bundle build` and `ruralz bundle validate --online` (the same process-level source as a file-mode Node, OQ-security-and-identity-8), since the pack makes the CLI a Plugin signature verifier under `enforce`.

Pack 8.14: state that offline keyless verification requires a transparency-log inclusion proof and a trusted timestamp in the Sigstore bundle, and that the Sigstore trusted root reaches Control-mode Nodes inside the root-signed anchor set.

Pack 8.2 Boot order step (3): add the `compromisedSince` exception that ADR-0017, Security and identity and Control plane and GitOps adopt (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-24, option (a)). A Control-mode Node does not boot a candidate or Last-Known-Good accepted from a removed key after `compromisedSince` and stays not ready until the Control Stream delivers. Today the ADR declares this exception to pack 8.2 and P9, but the pack does not contain it.
